               Pursuant to Advice Notice No. 317


Dear Ms. Sandoval,

        Pursuant to the Sua Sponte Order Vacating Procedural Schedule, Tolling Pending Deadlines, and
Requiring the Filing of an Amended Application (issued July 16, 2026) (“Sua Sponte Order”), and the
requirements of 17.1.210.11(B) and 17.9.530.9 NMAC, El Paso Electric Company (“EPE”) hereby
submits its amended request for an increase in retail electric rates. Accompanying this letter is EPE’s
Amended Application for Revision of its Retail Electric Rates, proposed tariffs , the matrix required by
the Sua Sponte Order, Rule 530 Schedules, EPE’s Direct Testimony and Exhibits, EPE’s work papers,
and a Certificate of Service. Each page of the filing is marked as “Amended Filing.” This amended rate
filing package supersedes and replaces the original Application (filed March 27, 2026).

       Advice Notice No. 317 was filed separately on March 27, 2026.

       EPE’s amended filing uses a twelve-month Base Period ending September 30, 2025, and a twelve-
month Historical Test Year Period as adjusted pursuant to Rule 530. EPE is seeking a rate increase to
cover a non-fuel base rate deficiency in revenue of $70.7 million, which is offset by a $0.241 million
reduction in miscellaneous service revenue, for a net revenue increase of $70.5 million.

        EPE is serving an electronic copy of this amended filing on the Attorney General, and all counsel
of record and pro se parties in this docket, pursuant to the requirements of the New Mexico Public
Regulation Commission’s interim working rules for PRCe360.

       Thank you for your assistance in this matter.

                            Purpose/Justification:
Construction of the Talavera Distribution Substation and related facilities
Purpose: The project consists of EPE constructing the substation and 0.3 mile access road; creating a 115kV transmission line in-and-out tap; upgrading
0.50 mile of an existing feeder, rebuilding 2.2 miles of an existing feeder to add a new feeder; and constructing two new feeders on a double circuit pole
line, 2.8 miles in length. The substation facilities consist of a six-position ring bus, two 50 MVA-115 kV/24 kV distribution transformers (100 MVA
total), two sets of switchgear, and a 30 MVAR capacitor bank.
Justification: The new substation is required to meet electrical demand, support future growth, and improve system reliability in the southern are of Doña
Ana County and City of Las Cruces. The existing Arroyo and Salopek Substations that serve the are and associated 24kV feeders are loaded to near
capacity. The new Talavera substation will back up these facilities, eliminating the risk of overloading feeders and significantly reducing the risk of
extended forced outages. EPE's Distribution Systems 2018 - 2027 Ten Year Expansion Plan identified the need for a new 115 kV/24kV substation to
replace the smaller Talavera temporary substation, currently in use. The new permanent substation will offset large amounts of load from neighboring
Salopek and Arroyo feeders and allow them to accommodate increasing loads in those areas. Additionally, the general area near and around Centennial
High School is in the process of being opened for development making this an emerging load growth area.
The addition of the 100MVA transformation capacity, the upgrade od an existing feeder, and the additional 24kV distribution feeders will allow EPE to
continue to reliably serve existing and future customer load requirements in Doña Ana County and the City of Las Cruces, New Mexico. The project is
necessary to improve EPE's ability to back feed to the surrounding distribution system in the event of an outage. The risk associated with no action will be
the inability, to serve any new load growth in this area and overloading of the existing distribution system, resulting in sustained outages to a large
number of customers in the areas, as well as damage to electrical equipment.

Cost Estimate Explanation Rule 17.5.440.8(D)(1)(a): The adjustment is attributable to supply chain disruptions and lead time extensions caused by the
COVID-19 pandemic; modified design standards; required equipment not included in the original estimate; and additional costs to meet Bureau of Land
Management requirements.

Undertaking Location/Description:
Location: Dona Ana County east of the City of Las Cruces in the Talavera area, and east of El Paso Electric Company’s (EPE’s) existing
345kV and 115kV transmission corridor. Specifically, it is located one mile south of Dripping Springs Road and west of Achenback
Canyon Road, approximately 0.3 mile in the SE¼ of Section 19, Township 23 South, Range 3 East, New Mexico Prime Meridian.
Substation coordinates are Latitude 32° 17’ 17.628" N and Longitude 106° 40’ 10.4376"W.
Description: The project consists of: (1) constructing the substation and 0.3 mile access road; (2) creating a 115kV transmission line
in-and-out tap; (3) upgrading 0.50 mile of an existing feeder; (4) rebuilding 2.2 miles an existing feeder to add a new feeder; and (5)
constructing two new feeders on a double circuit pole line, 2.8 miles in length. The substation facilities consist of a six-position ring
bus, two 50 MVA-115 kV/24 kV distribution transformers (100 MVA total), two sets of switchgear, and a 30 MVAR capacitor bank.
Approximately 0.10 mile of new transmission line will be constructed to connect the substation to the existing Arroyo to Anthony
115kV transmission line, forming the 115kV Arroyo to Talavera and l l5kV Talavera to Anthony transmission lines. Approximately
0.50 mile of an existing 24kV three phase single circuit distribution feeder will be rebuilt to replace the existing #2ACSR conductor with
a 795AAC conductor with 336ACSR static to increase capacity. EPE will replace the existing poles on that line. The poles of an existing
2.2 miles of 24kV feeder will be replaced to allow the attachment of a new 24kV - 795AAC feeder to increase capacity. The conductor
on that existing feeder will remain the same. The 2.28 miles of new 24kV feeders will be constructed as a three-phase double
circuit line using a 795AAC conductor with 336ACSR static. The proposed substation, the 115kV transmission line in-and-out tap, and
the majority of the distribution feeders will be constructed on Federal land managed by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM). The
BLM has granted EPE the necessary Grants of Right of Way to construct all facilities located on Federal land. EPE will acquire
distribution utility easement for the approximate 0.50 mile segment of new feeder not located on Federal land.
